body:
WHAT
Durations on screen are the engine's own measurements.
- Protocol (optional fields, so an older engine or frontend still works; tui/src/protocol.ts mirrors the fields the TUI reads — turn_started.at and turn_finished.at): turn_started, tool_call_started, tool_call_finished and turn_finished carry at (epoch ms, the engine's clock when it emitted the frame). TaskItem carries startedAt (when its status first became in_progress) and completedAt (when it became completed; cleared if it is reopened). A task completed straight from pending gets no startedAt, so no duration is invented for it.
- The task store stamps those times on status changes and persists them, so a resumed session's tasks keep their durations.
- Desktop: the task rail takes a task's start and end from startedAt/completedAt when present (else, as before, from when the flip was seen); a tool row starts at tool_call_started.at and ends at tool_call_finished.at; the turn timer starts at turn_started.at. A live timer still reads now minus the engine's start — same machine, same clock, and there is no other "now".
- The shape is option (a) of the plan: a stamp on the frames that need one, not a transport field on every frame.

WHY
Field test 2026-09-23, findings R-2, U-03, U-04, U-05. After T01's backlog the rail showed 7 s for a two-minute task and 16 s for a seventeen-minute one, and the turn timer stood at 26:53: every time on screen was Date.now() at the moment the renderer HANDLED a frame, and no engine frame carried a time. The main process log had every task_list_updated at the right moment.

WHERE
engine/protocol/src/types.ts (TaskItem, turn_started, tool_call_started, tool_call_finished) and tui/src/protocol.ts. engine/core/src/state/taskStore.ts — update(). engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — the three emits. app/renderer/modules/tasks.js onTaskListUpdated(); app/renderer/modules/views.js startNowLine(at); app/renderer/modules/landing.js onTurnStarted(event), onToolCallStarted(), onToolCallFinished(); app/renderer/modules/stream.js finishToolRow(…, finishedAt).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. (fs) A real engine turn: turn_started, tool_call_started and tool_call_finished carry at, in order, within the turn's wall-clock span.
2. (fs) The task store: in_progress stamps startedAt, completed stamps completedAt, reopening clears completedAt, pending → completed stamps no startedAt; the times survive a reload of the store from disk.
3. (ui) In the real app, a task started 120 s ago and completed 5 s ago (engine times) delivered now shows 1m55s; a tool row whose frames are 30 s apart but delivered together shows 30s; the turn timer of a turn that started 26½ minutes ago reads 26:3x, not 0:00.

ADDED 2026-09-24 (audit follow-up):
- (fs) Each call's tool_call_finished is sent when THAT call settles, not when its batch does; the stamps are ordered only by turn start ≤ call start ≤ call finish ≤ turn end (two parallel calls may finish in either order).
- (ui) The work group spans its first call's engine start to the turn's engine end (turn_finished.at); a task the engine stamps is timed by its stamps alone, so a reused task id never borrows an earlier session's start.
